passage: Advisor's note. On Saturday night I watched Tenzin, founder of a small delivery app, answer critics on a public thread. A customer had complained about late orders. Tenzin replied point by point, called the customer's numbers 'made up', and hinted that the customer was paid by a rival. Two others joined in. By Sunday morning someone had posted screenshots of the exchange on a bigger page; the thread drew more views than the original complaint had in a month, and three users wrote that they were leaving. On Monday I sat with Tenzin and Jasleen from support. I asked what the customer had actually said, and Tenzin found it was partly right about the late orders. We agreed Tenzin would stop replying for now and Jasleen would collect the facts.

qa.q: What had the original customer complained about?
qa.a: The customer had complained about late orders.

qa.q: What was Tenzin probably feeling while writing the replies?
qa.a: Tenzin was probably defensive and hurt, since every point was fought and the customer was accused of being paid by a rival.

qa.q: What could Tenzin have done instead of arguing?
qa.a: Tenzin could have replied once, thanked the customer, and said what was being checked about the late orders, without arguing over motives.

qa.q: How might the three users who said they were leaving have seen the thread?
qa.a: They may have seen a company that argues rather than listens, and doubted they would get help when something went wrong.

grounding: Shows a founder arguing point by point with critics and attacking their motives, so screenshots spread and the argument draws more attention than the complaint.

passage:
Thursday night
I made it so much worse. Yesterday a customer named Rukmini posted that our delivery was late three times and our support ignored her. Honestly, two of those were her address mistakes. So I replied publicly, point by point. Then she replied, and I replied again, and I wrote that she was 'probably paid by a competitor'.
That was the line. Someone screenshotted it. By this morning it was everywhere, with our logo, under the title 'Founder attacks customer'. Our original problem was three late deliveries. Now it's forty thousand people who think I'm a bully. My co-founder hasn't spoken to me since lunch.
I can't delete it now; deleting will look worse. I'm going to write a real apology tomorrow, and I'm handing all public replies to someone calmer than me.
Baljeet

qa.q: Under what title did the screenshot spread?
How is Baljeet feeling on Thursday night?
qa.a: Baljeet feels ashamed and regretful, seeing that the attack drew far more attention than the complaint.

qa.q: What approach could Baljeet have used instead of arguing point by point?
qa.a: A short public reply acknowledging the problem and offering to sort the details privately would have stopped the fight before it grew.

qa.q: How might Rukmini feel seeing the screenshot spread?
qa.a: Rukmini may feel vindicated but also exposed, having been publicly accused of being paid by a competitor.

grounding: It shows a founder arguing with a critic point by point and attacking her motives, so screenshots spread and the fight draws more attention than the complaint.

Sachin: Nilesh. stop replying to that thread. please
Nilesh: he's lying. our app didn't lose his data. I'm just correcting facts
Sachin: you've replied 11 times. you called him 'clueless' twice
Nilesh: because he is
Sachin: someone just screenshotted your 'clueless' reply. it's on three other pages now
Nilesh: so? people will see I'm right
Sachin: people see a founder mocking a customer. the original post had 40 likes. your replies have 2,000 shares
Nilesh: ...
Sachin: the data question can be checked privately. I've messaged him asking for his account email
Nilesh: fine. I'll stop
Sachin: and tomorrow we post one calm reply. I'll draft it

qa.q: How many times had Nilesh replied?

qa.a: It suggests Nilesh is stunned and deflated, suddenly seeing how badly the replies backfired.

qa.q: What is the better approach Sachin suggests?
qa.a: Checking the data question privately with the customer and posting one calm public reply the next day.

qa.q: How does the thread look to Sachin?
qa.a: Sachin sees a small complaint turning into widespread damage and is anxious to stop it quickly.

grounding: It shows a founder arguing with critics and mocking a customer, so screenshots spread and the argument draws far more attention than the complaint.
